handed_forward: record the per-step pre-drift error stream of (i) a standalone HAT and (ii) one tree inside the ARF, on matched seeds and magnitudes, then calibrate both to one false alarm per warm-up and re-derive the factor

measurable_substitute.reading: a mismatch factor far from 1 says the two marginals differ, so the measured Hydra factor mixes a marginal effect with an ensemble-minimum effect and must not be published as a single number
measurable_substitute.statement: the marginal assimilation the manuscript makes silently -- F_hat, the HAT's law, used as the law of a tree INSIDE the ARF -- is testable on committed data through the slowest member: E[tau_(10)] measured on runs.parquet against E[max of 10 draws from F_hat]

question: the Hydra factor compares tau_HAT (M = 1) against tau_ARF (M = 10) at a COMMON NOMINAL internal-clock setting; S2 measured that equal-false-alarm calibration hands the ARF a threshold 6.3x lower than the HT, so part of any measured factor may be a calibration difference

sensitivity_bound_from_available_varianc.reading: the only committed pre-drift variance contrast is adaptive-ARF (arm full) against non-adaptive bagged HT (arm static), both at M = 10. It bounds the effect of ADAPTATION on the pre-drift error stream, not the effect of ENSEMBLE SIZE, and is reported as a bound of the wrong contrast rather than as a substitute for the missing one.

verdict: NOT PRODUCED -- the committed artifacts do not carry the inputs
why: no committed artifact records the pre-drift error STREAM of a single tree, either standalone or inside the ARF. R6 commits tau_hat only (4 columns, no e_pre); runs.parquet commits e_pre for ensemble arms at n_models = 10 exclusively (arms present: ['frozen', 'full', 'no_swap', 'static']); no traces.parquet is committed. The equal-budget threshold is therefore not computable without a new campaign.
